General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: On the arrest of Informer TV owner and editor-in-chief Dragan J. Vucicevic: Has the reckoning with Serbia's pro-Vucic media machine begun?

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1062 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Break their ribs," shouted the man in the studio during a live TV broadcast.
  • Vucicevic, editor-in-chief of the channel Informer TV, and he was urging police officers to use force against demonstrators during a major student protest in June last year.
  • On November 25, Vucicevic was arrested by the police on suspicion of causing panic and disorder and obstructing justice.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"Beat them! Break their ribs," shouted the man in the studio during a live TV broadcast.

The man in question was Dragan J. Vucicevic, editor-in-chief of the channel Informer TV, and he was urging police officers to use force against demonstrators during a major student protest in June last year.

On November 25, Vucicevic was arrested by the police on suspicion of causing panic and disorder and obstructing justice. According to the authorities, his appearances "created an atmosphere of public lynching" and he labelled 97 citizens as enemies of the state.

The authorities cite instances where he described protesters as "scum," "hyenas" and "vultures" and spread claims that the students were preparing a "bloodbath" and a "civil war.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The prosecution indicates that between 2023 and 2026, Vucicevic systematically used Informer TV to conduct a campaign that incited hatred and targeted political opponents of the previous government, activists and independent journalists.

Vucicevic's arrest comes at a time of profound political change in Serbia.

Following the Student List's victory in the parliamentary election in late October and the end of the Serbian Progressive Party's (SNS) 14-year rule, questions have arisen about the accountability of people who were part of the previous political and institutional system.

Critics have described Vucicevic as the mouthpiece of former President Aleksandar Vucic — a man who noted publicly what the president was thinking but could not say himself because of the office he held.

Sources indicate that "He [Vucicevic] is someone who stopped being a journalist a long time ago, and I think he crossed the line of being merely a propagandist some time ago. He was, in fact, a weapon in the hands of Aleksandar Vucic and his party," said Ivana Stevanovic of the Slavko Curuvija Foundation, a Belgrade-based organization named after a Serbian journalist who was killed in 1999 that provides media support and fights for press freedom.

Stevanovic told DW that Vucicevic used his media platforms to "target and endanger people, spread falsehoods that threatened their safety," all as part of a campaign against political opponents, journalists and media outlets who were critical of the government's record.

According to recent reports, "This man demonstrated a female student's intimate photographs live on air. He stalked people. He had his notorious 'Viewer Intelligence Service,' which secretly followed people and filmed them in their everyday lives, then turned that material into disgusting reports," she stated.

According to recent reports, "We had calls for violence, threats and insults against prosecutors who were doing their jobs and judges who were issuing lawful rulings, expressed in indescribable language. We had wiretapping, recordings of conversations in restaurants presented as conspiracies to overthrow the state. Media outlets and journalists were accused of plotting to assassinate the president, while their reporting was portrayed as treason and selling out Kosovo," she told DW, adding that "the entire television channel is one major criminal offence.".

The Regulatory Authority for Electronic Media (REM) has already issued several warnings and temporarily halted the broadcasting of certain programs on Informer TV.

Journalists' and media associations, civil society organizations and representatives of academia have rolled out an initiative to have the channel's broadcasting license revoked.

According to the Slavko Curuvija Foundation, more than 1,000 court cases concerning the protection of reputation and honor have been brought against Informer in recent years.

"Of the cases concluded over the past three years, courts upheld the claims in 92% of them," noted Stevanovic. "Compensation was awarded to people whose rights had been violated. Informer even paid damages to the same individuals several times for the same lies, which it kept publishing about them. None of these financial penalties made them stop.".

Industry observers note that on one occasion, Dragan J. Vucicevic himself asked REM to impose a financial penalty on him rather than ban part of his program.

Money, it seems, was not a problem for Insajder Tim, the organization behind all Informer media platforms (a daily tabloid newspaper, a television channel and an online portal).

According to an investigation by Raskrikavanje, a fact-checking website that monitors the output of Serbian media, Insajder Tim, received around €273,000 ($299,000) in public funds in 2024 alone through public procurement contracts, advertising and media project funding.

Representatives of the Student List have claimed that the state-owned telecommunications firm Telekom Srbija paid Informer between €500,000 and €700,000 a month.

Telekom Srbija, which also owns a cable network distributing television channels to millions of users in Serbia, cited business confidentiality when asked about the details of its cooperation with Informer.

Vucicevic and his lawyers reject the accusations.

The defense argues that the proceedings amount to punishing someone for words they have spoken and raise questions about the boundary between freedom of expression and criminal liability.

According to recent reports, former President Aleksandar Vucic stated Vucicevic had been arrested solely because of his journalistic work. SNS lawmakers walked out of a parliamentary session following news of the arrest and gathered outside the police station where the Informer editor was being held.

Stevanovic maintains that by arresting Vucicevic, Serbia is fulfilling its international obligations, including those arising from the European Convention on Human Rights and international conventions protecting civil and political rights.

"What constitutes a call for violence and a threat to democracy, security and health must be sanctioned and removed from the public sphere," she stated.

Vucicevic has been remanded in custody for 30 days.

The offence of causing panic and disorder through the media carries a prison sentence of between six months and five years.

Stevanovic points out, however, that the outcome of the case is not certain because the executive branch, the police and the Ministry of the Interior formally remain under the control of the outgoing government until such time as the Student List forms a latest cabinet.

It has been revealed that "What is happening now could be an internal power struggle within their own ranks, or an attempt by some prosecutors to clean up their records and ingratiate themselves with the new authorities, assuming what their wishes and intentions regarding Informer might be," she mentioned. "Or it could be a serious manipulation, a staged arrest designed to portray Serbia abroad as a country carrying out revolutionary terror, which, of course, is not true.".

📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

Can you play GTA 6 from an external hard drive on PS5 or Xbox Series X/S?

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (305 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rockstar’s behemoth takes up a lot of storage space.
  • Grand Theft Auto 6 is the biggest game of the year by some distance, having racked up $3.79 billion in pre-orders and day-one sales.
  • It has been revealed that there will be many other folks who want to play the game and haven't had a chance to jump in yet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar’s behemoth takes up a lot of storage space.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is the biggest game of the year by some distance, having racked up $3.79 billion in pre-orders and day-one sales. On PlayStation 5 alone, more than 39 million unique players took control of dual protagonists Jason and Lucia on opening weekend, making it the biggest game debut in the 32-year history of PlayStation.

It has been revealed that there will be many other folks who want to play the game and haven't had a chance to jump in yet. One thing they should note is that, with a hefty install size, GTA 6 will take up a significant chunk of their PS5 or Xbox Series X/S storage space.

In a recent development, you might be wondering whether you can install GTA 6 on an external hard drive to avoid having to delete other games and data from your console. You can move GTA 6 to your external storage when you're not playing it. However, to run the game locally, you'll need to have it installed on your system's built-in storage, an SDD you've installed in your PS5 or a compatible NVMe expansion card that's plugged into your Xbox.

It has been revealed that as with many other recent games, GTA 6 needs to take advantage of the fast-loading capabilities of the PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. The consoles are unable to load data for these titles quickly enough from an external hard drive over a USB connection. For the same reason, disc-based PS5 and Xbox Series X games are installed onto system storage before you can play them. The PS5 can run PS4 games from external storage, though. Likewise, an Xbox Series X/S can run older Xbox One and Xbox 360 titles directly from an external hard drive.

    #219237. Todoist confirms 6% of customers’ details were stolen in data breach

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (527 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 TechCrunch ↗ Open Full Page

    Todoist confirms 6% of customers’ details were stolen in data breach

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (527 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, task management app Todoist mentioned on Tuesday that a hacker gained access to its production systems and stole customer data, including email IDs, password hashes, and account creation dates.
    • Todoist remarked the attacker used stolen credentials to access the firm’s version control system and source code between November 22 and 23.
    • Recent findings suggest that the hacker downloaded credentials of early Todoist customers whose passwords were stored using an older hashing method, but didn’t change any source code, the organization said.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, task management app Todoist mentioned on Tuesday that a hacker gained access to its production systems and stole customer data, including email IDs, password hashes, and account creation dates. The tech giant said around 6% of its customers were affected and blamed stolen credentials for the breach.

    Todoist remarked the attacker used stolen credentials to access the firm’s version control system and source code between November 22 and 23. The hacker then changed employee access controls and reached the app’s cloud infrastructure via an employee’s work account.

    Recent findings suggest that the hacker downloaded credentials of early Todoist customers whose passwords were stored using an older hashing method, but didn’t change any source code, the organization said. Todoist said it has blocked the attack path and reset passwords as a mitigation step, as well as disabled the Todoist for Outlook email add-on.

    For a small number of people, about 0.001% of its userbase, the hacker also searched through tasks, comments, and attachment names to look for credentials for other services, like API keys and access tokens.

    The hacker also pulled Todoist API tokens and Slack integration tokens, and looked for emails, addresses, and attachment file names through the Todoist for Outlook extension if it was connected to accounts and had permission to read emails.

    Recent findings suggest that the manufacturer noted it has sent a notice to those affected and asked them to reset their credentials and change their login details in other places with the same password. The company is asking consumers to also enhancement API tokens, reconnect integrations, and revoke or replace any access keys, recovery phrases, or credentials they had stored in Todoist comments.

    Todoist said it has also reset its internal access structure and how remote command execution works in its cloud environment to prevent such incidents in the future.

    Todoist’s founder and CEO Amir Salihefendić apologized to users about the incident on X, and noted the company will take a closer look at why it happened.

    The to-do app’s data breach is the latest in a burgeoning list of data breaches in which hackers use stolen credentials to access data and systems at enterprises. So far this year, we’ve seen several companies fall victim to this form of attack, including Uber and Klue.

    Uganda to withdraw troops from DR Congo town amid diplomatic row

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (591 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The planned withdrawal will end Uganda's nearly two-year campaign against ADF militants in Lubero.
    • Uganda has announced looks to withdraw its troops from a town in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo within two weeks, as diplomatic tensions escalate between the two neighbours.
    • The troops will hand over security in Lubero, in North Kivu province, to Congolese forces after nearly two years of military operations, the Ugandan army said in a statement on Friday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The planned withdrawal will end Uganda's nearly two-year campaign against ADF militants in Lubero.

    Uganda has announced looks to withdraw its troops from a town in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo within two weeks, as diplomatic tensions escalate between the two neighbours.

    The troops will hand over security in Lubero, in North Kivu province, to Congolese forces after nearly two years of military operations, the Ugandan army said in a statement on Friday.

    The announcement comes days after DR Congo summoned Uganda's top diplomat in Kinshasa over controversial social media posts by Uganda's military chief, Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, who is the son of President Yoweri Museveni.

    The Ugandan military did not give a reason for the withdrawal or say whether it was linked to the diplomatic row.

    What are Ugandan forces doing in DR Congo?

    The Uganda People's Defence Forces (UPDF) were deployed to Lubero to pursue fighters from the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) Islamist group fleeing joint military operations elsewhere in eastern DR Congo.

    The ADF, which originated in Uganda in the 1990s, is affiliated to the Islamic State and has been blamed for numerous deadly attacks on civilians in both countries.

    Uganda first deployed troops to eastern DR Congo under the current joint military campaign in November 2021, following a series of bomb attacks in the Ugandan capital, Kampala.

    Ugandan army spokesperson Col Chris Magezi said that the joint military campaign, known as Operation Shujaa, would continue elsewhere in DR Congo.

    The planned withdrawal applies only to Lubero town.

    Five years into the joint offensive, the ADF remains DR Congo's deadliest armed group, despite a significant decline in its activities in Uganda, according to the conflict monitoring organisation Armed Conflict Location & Event Data (Acled).

    John Ngono, Acled's DR Congo analyst, stated the group was killing an average of four civilians a day and had expanded into previously unaffected parts of eastern DR Congo.

    He said the findings suggested that "Operation Shujaa may have improved security in Uganda while shifting the geographical impact of violence within the DRC".

    Acled notes the group has not carried out an attack in Uganda since June 2025, but its growing interest in mineral resources in DR Congo could help finance its operations and sustain its ability to threaten both countries.

    The planned withdrawal comes amid strained relations between Uganda and DR Congo, despite years of close military co-operation.

    Earlier this week, Gen Kainerugaba appeared to endorse a rebel takeover of Walikale, a mineral-rich territory in eastern DR Congo, threatening that Ugandan troops would seize it themselves if the rebels failed to do so.

    The Congolese foreign ministry described his remarks as "particularly serious" and demanded that Uganda clarify its official position and take steps to prevent similar incidents.

    Gen Kainerugaba also defended Uganda's military presence in eastern DR Congo, insisting it was driven by security concerns.

    The planned withdrawal comes amid renewed fighting between Congolese forces and rebels in the wider Lubero territory, raising fresh concerns about the safety of civilians.

    Eastern DR Congo has endured decades of conflict involving dozens of armed groups, with millions of people forced to flee their homes.

    #219235. The FCC has authorized SpaceX to deploy 1 million satellites

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (654 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

    The FCC has authorized SpaceX to deploy 1 million satellites

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (654 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In an extraordinary decision, the Federal Communications Commission on Wednesday granted SpaceX conditional authorization to deploy a constellation of up to 1 million Starmind satellites designed to serve as orbital data centers.
    • If fully deployed, this constellation would increase the number of satellites in orbit by roughly 50-fold.
    • “The United States is moving decisively to ensure that this breakthrough technology creates opportunity, drives investment, and delivers lasting benefits for the American people,” FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said in a statement on Wednesday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In an extraordinary decision, the Federal Communications Commission on Wednesday granted SpaceX conditional authorization to deploy a constellation of up to 1 million Starmind satellites designed to serve as orbital data centers.

    If fully deployed, this constellation would increase the number of satellites in orbit by roughly 50-fold.

    “The United States is moving decisively to ensure that this breakthrough technology creates opportunity, drives investment, and delivers lasting benefits for the American people,” FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said in a statement on Wednesday. “This action opens a bold new frontier for the computing infrastructure needed to power America’s leadership and growth.”.

    The decision, announced a day before the Thanksgiving holiday in the United States, represents a major regulatory victory for SpaceX and its founder, Elon Musk, who has allied himself with the Trump administration.

    Recent findings suggest that this announcement clears a major hurdle to deploying data centers in space, although it does not establish that orbital data centers are technically or economically viable. Nevertheless, the FCC authorization appears designed to give the company wide latitude as it works through these remaining issues.

    Industry observers note that for example, SpaceX has seven years to deploy a single operational Starmind satellite under the order. SpaceX has until November 2035 to deploy 100,000 operational satellites, and November 2040 for the full constellation. SpaceX, therefore, has a 14-year regulatory runway to deploy the most ambitious industrial project ever approved for spaceflight.

    Industry observers note that the authorization includes some conditional aspects. SpaceX has proposed operating in six orbits, ranging from 550 km to about 1,000 km. The company sought a waiver from FCC rules to allow satellites above 600 km to be disposed of into “Earth disposal orbits or heliocentric orbits.” That is, instead of burning them up in Earth’s atmosphere, SpaceX wants the flexibility to move retired satellites into other orbits around Earth, or potentially into orbit around the Sun.

    The FCC did not grant this waiver request “because SpaceX has not provided sufficient information for the Commission to determine whether its alternative disposal methods are compliant with the Commission’s requirements.” The organization will need to obtain a waiver before deploying any Starmind satellites that are not intended to be disposed of via atmospheric reentry.

    Recent findings suggest that however, in other ways the FCC appears to have been incredibly lenient with SpaceX. This is particularly the case with environmental concerns raised by numerous parties that commented on SpaceX’s application to the FCC.

    Half a dozen organizations, such as the Secure World Foundation and American Astronomical Society, raised concerns about deploying so many satellites into orbit, citing collision risks, orbital debris, atmospheric pollution from so many satellite reentries, impacts on astronomical observations, and more. The FCC also received approximately 1,500 public comments concerning SpaceX’s application.

    Some of these environmental issues, the FCC said, lay beyond the scope of its review. For example, on concerns about the environmental implications of thousands or potentially tens of thousands of rocket releases, the FCC said, “Potential concerns related to the emissions of rocket launches and the subsequent impacts on the human environment as an indirect result of the Starmind system are outside of the Commission’s purview.”.

    The FCC also rejected calls for further environmental scrutiny of pollution from satellite reentries, including concerns about aluminum oxides and their potential effects on the ozone layer. “Other concerns, including impacts on the atmosphere caused by satellites burning up on re-entry, remain speculative and not supported in the record,” the FCC authorization states.

    As part of its decision, the FCC cited a significant policy change adopted in October, when the agency concluded that space-based activities generally fall outside its obligations under the National Environmental Policy Act. The FCC reasoned that as these activities occur beyond US territory, they don’t constitute federal actions requiring environmental review. As a result, the agency declined to conduct a comprehensive environmental assessment of SpaceX’s Starmind constellation.

    • The outage has been impacting both the manufacturer’s website and mobile app, TechCrunch confirmed.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, U.S. insurer Allstate has been experiencing a tech outage since Monday morning, leaving customers nationwide unable to access their accounts, review their policy information, file claims, pay their bills, and more, just ahead of the U.S. Thanksgiving holidays.

    The outage has been impacting both the manufacturer’s website and mobile app, TechCrunch confirmed.

    Industry observers note that the breakdown follows a report from earlier this month that Allstate was planning to lay off up to 10% of its staff as part of an AI-driven efficiency push. (The manufacturer had not confirmed the report, which was attributed to unnamed sources.).

    Allstate’s outage is the latest in a series of disruptions to services such as Microsoft Outlook and Teams, the airlines, Apple Pay, and several banks. Trump administration officials have stated the outages are not being caused by cyberattacks, but are rather being caused by a recent set of upgrades to systems, many of which run on older technology. Those systems are now in need of more frequent security and bug fixes as AI makes it easier and faster to discover vulnerabilities.

    Downdetector, a crowdsourced outage-reporting website, reveals consumers began reporting Allstate’s outage from Monday morning. However, the tech giant hasn’t yet issued a formal statement about the disruption, what’s causing it, or when it may be resolved. In the meantime, local insurance agents have been fielding calls and emails from customers who aren’t able to use the company’s online services.

    Sources indicate that the timing of the outage is particularly bad given that Thanksgiving is a substantial travel holiday in the U.S., which means there will be car accidents. Customers will be left without a way to get in touch with their auto insurer to file claims and get roadside assistance through Allstate’s app.

    Allstate did not immediately return a request for comment. On Wednesday evening, after publication, the manufacturer sent the following statement (below). It did not answer questions about the outage’s cause or planned resolution.

    Allstate customers can reach us in many ways, including online, by phone and through local offices. Some access has been restricted over the last 48 hours, but we continue to be available for customers and respond to and settle claims. To the extent service interruptions impact a customer’s ability to make a payment, they won’t lose coverage or be charged late fees.

    Updated after publication with Allstate’s comment.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Emmanuel Macron noted it would be a "strategic mistake" to reduce EU spending.
    • European Union (EU) leaders have deferred negotiations on its long-term budget after tensions surfaced over the bloc's spending priorities and aid for Ukraine.
    • Tense talks on the 2028-34 budget ended after 12 hours on Thursday at a summit in Brussels, with some members walking out of negotiations that will resume in December.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Emmanuel Macron noted it would be a "strategic mistake" to reduce EU spending.

    European Union (EU) leaders have deferred negotiations on its long-term budget after tensions surfaced over the bloc's spending priorities and aid for Ukraine.

    Tense talks on the 2028-34 budget ended after 12 hours on Thursday at a summit in Brussels, with some members walking out of negotiations that will resume in December.

    Divisions were largely split along the lines of countries, including France and Italy, wanting to approve a higher-spending proposal against those advocating for financial restraint, with Germany chief among them.

    Many members want the budget locked in ahead of several high-stakes elections held across Europe in 2027, including in France.

    Countries remain divided over a proposal to provide Ukraine with an additional loan of â¬45bn (Â£37.6bn), split between non-military and military funding.

    Slovakia, the Czech Republic and Hungary have objected to the loan, but German Chancellor Frederich Merz remarked uniform EU agreement was a condition for approving the broader budget.

    "I stand by my view that aid for Ukraine must be supported by the European Union as a whole," Merz told reporters.

    "The European Union comprises of 27 member states, not 23 or 24.".

    Bulgaria, which previously opposed the proposal, mentioned it would agree to fund part of the loan that commits non-military financial support to Kyiv, marking a small sign of progress emerging from the special summit of the European Council.

    EU members have been wrangling over the long-term budget after the European Commission submitted a â¬2tn proposal earlier this year, with some countries objecting to high levels of spending.

    Those advocating higher spending want the funds to future-proof industries such as farming and invest in regional development. Fiscally cautious countries want to avoid amassing ballooning debt.

    Thursday's talks were set up by the European Council to unblock the impasse, with a proposal to reduce spending by approximately â¬220bn to â¬230bn.

    Under the current proposal, the budget totals â¬1.582tn, which includes â¬140bn to repay pandemic-era borrowing.

    Four countries wanting to rein in the budget, including Denmark and Austria, walked out of negotiations after several hours of meetings.

    Merz said there was "fresh movement" towards reducing the size of the EU budget, though he added "we are not there yet" when he confirmed that a new round of negotiations would not take place in Brussels on Friday.

    European budgets requires approval from all 27 countries, with each country effectively holding veto power.

    French President Emmanuel Macron said it would be a "strategic mistake" to lower long-term spending.

    France's forthcoming presidential election came into focus during the EU budget talks, with frontrunner Marine Le Pen calling the talks an "underhanded political manoeuvring to thwart the democratic will of the French people".

    Last month, Le Pen confirmed she would significantly reduce French aid to Ukraine and EU contributions if she were to win the presidency.

    Macron addressed Le Pen's remarks on the sidelines of the Brussels summit, saying: "It is an odd kind of arrogance to behave as if she is already in charge of France's destiny because, as things stand, she has not been elected.".

    Once the talks concluded, the European Council confirmed a two-day summit on 17 and 18 December would revive budget negotiations.

    Spanish economist Pablo HernÃ¡ndez de Cos was also named as the next President of the European Central Bank, replacing Christine Lagarde from February 2027.

    According to recent reports, multiple gadgets from Engadget's Best of 2026 list are already on sale, including Samsung's flagship foldable smartphone and Apple's ultra-popular (and cute) entry-level laptop. Online retailers like Amazon seem to offer the steepest discounts, but buying directly from the manufacturer can also net you extra savings, particularly if you have a device you want to trade in. If you don't see what you want on sale now, worry not: New deals will continue to pop up throughout Thanksgiving and Black Friday. In the meantime, here's a selection of what you can save on now.

    Apple has had a massive year of product releases, both in terms of wholly latest product categories and old standbys it's finally shown some love. The firm is running its own Black Friday sale on its website through November 30, which can net you Apple gift cards ranging from $25 to $300 depending on the product you purchase, but you can also find some excellent deals on Amazon.

    According to recent reports, the colorful new MacBook Neo, Apple's first computer powered by an iPhone chip (the A18 Pro) and its first relatively budget-friendly laptop, is on sale at Amazon for $649, $50 off its normal $699 starting price. The Neo made a significant splash when it introduced in March because it offered some of the premium benefits of Apple's more expensive computers at an affordable $599, a price Apple unfortunately raised to $699 in June due to the high cost of memory and storage. This discount helps recapture some of that original magic.

    If you'd prefer something more powerful, you can also opt for the newly introduced M5 MacBook Air, which is on sale on Amazon for $1,049, $250 off its normal $1,299 price. The new M5 chip is the main upgrade this year, and it offers more than enough power for basic work, with extra headroom for AI tools and light gaming.

    Recent findings suggest that arguably the best Apple deals so far, though, are the current discounts on the AirPods Pro 3 and the Apple Watch Series 12. You can purchase Apple's high-end wireless earbuds for just $149 on Amazon, a 40 percent discount on the usual $249 Apple charges. Meanwhile, Apple's latest smartwatch — which features a redesigned health sensor — is going for $299 on Amazon, $100 off its normal $399 price.

    Like Apple, Google is offering some exclusive deals on its website if you're interested in saving on accessories or getting an even better deal on a trade-in. The bulk of the manufacturer's discounts on smartphones and smartwatches are being reflected across retailers, though.

    For example, both the Pixel 11 and Pixel 11 Pro are on sale on Amazon. The base Pixel 11, which comes in new colors, includes more storage and has a collection of AI-powered camera features, is on sale on Amazon for $699, over 20 percent off its normal $899 starting price. You can also get the Pixel 11 Pro, Google's higher-end model with its new HiLight customizable notification light, for $749 on Amazon, a $350 discount on its usual $1,099 starting price.

    In a recent development, if you've already got an Android phone and are looking for a good smartwatch, you can get a Pixel Watch 5, Google's latest smartwatch, on sale on Amazon for $330, $100 off its $430 starting price. The latest smartwatch offers easy access to Gemini, improved GPS tracking for outdoor workouts and new gestures for controlling the watch without using the touchscreen.

    Industry observers note that while Apple's first foldable, the iPhone Duo, is the hot commodity heading into the holiday season, it doesn't yet have an easy-to-snag Black Friday deal. You can get Engadget's favorite foldable of the year for a healthy discount, though.The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 features a upcoming, more passport-shaped form factor and one of the company's best anti-glare displays. It's also available on Amazon for $1,550, a still eye-popping price, but cheaper than the $1,900 Samsung usually charges. If you're on Android and Duo-curious, the Z Fold 8 is the better foldable anyway.

    It has been revealed that for anyone all-in on Gemini and Google's Pixel ecosystem, the less beloved but still competently made Pixel 11 Pro Fold is on sale on Amazon for $1,649. That's a $250 discount on what's usually a $1,899 foldable, and you still get Google's polished take on Android and extensive software support.

    According to recent reports, if you're building out a home office or setting up your first PC gaming rig, you'll want a monitor you're willing to stare at for hours on end. The Alienware 39 5K not only offers ample screen real estate with its 39-inch, ever-so-slightly curved display, but also a wonderfully bright and vivid OLED panel that can switch between 5K 165Hz and 1080p+ 330Hz modes with a button push.

    According to recent reports, the monitor is on sale directly through Dell's website for $1,000, $100 off what Dell normally charges. If you want the best experience for gaming and staring at Microsoft Word, it's hard to go wrong with the Alienware 39 5K.
